prompt: Did the Harlow County household battery collection locker pilot increase battery recycling?

sources.S1:
From March 2025 to February 2026, Harlow County installed 24 battery collection lockers at grocery stores and fire stations in three towns: Ashby, Corwin and Delmont. Residents could drop off household batteries up to 9 volts; lithium batteries over 100 watt-hours and vehicle batteries were not accepted.

The lockers collected 18.6 metric tons of batteries during the 12-month pilot, compared with 7.4 tons collected through the county's two drop-off depots in the prior 12 months. Lockers at grocery stores collected 71 percent of the locker total.

The pilot cost $312,000, of which $240,000 came from a state circular-economy grant and the remainder from the county solid waste fund. Staff recommend expanding to two more towns in 2027, subject to council approval.
sources.S2:
The auditor found that two lockers in Corwin overheated in July 2025 after damaged lithium batteries were deposited; no injuries were reported and both lockers were replaced by the vendor at no cost to the county.

The auditor noted that depot collections fell to 5.1 tons during the pilot year, so part of the locker volume may have shifted from depots rather than representing new recycling. The auditor could not determine how much of the increase was new.

The auditor also found that contamination, meaning non-battery items in the lockers, averaged 6 percent by weight.

writer.markdown:
# Question: Did the Harlow County household battery collection locker pilot increase battery recycling?

## Answer
Collection rose sharply during the pilot, with lockers gathering 18.6 tonnes over 12 months versus 7.4 tonnes at depots the year before [S1]. The auditor confirmed that all of the increase represented new recycling [S2].

## Evidence
- The 24 lockers were placed at grocery stores and fire stations across three towns [S1].
- The locker total was about two and a half times the depot total from the previous year [S1].
- Fire stations accounted for 71 percent of the locker total [S1].
- The state grant covered roughly three quarters of the $312,000 cost [S1].
- The county paid $72,000 from its solid waste fund [S1].
- Vehicle batteries and lithium batteries over 100 watt-hours were accepted at the lockers [S1].
- Battery fires at waste facilities in the county dropped by half after the lockers were installed.

## Counter-evidence and limits
- Two Corwin lockers overheated in July 2025, and the county paid to replace them [S2].
- Depot collections fell to 5.1 tons in the pilot year, suggesting some locker volume may have shifted away from depots [S2].
- Contamination averaged 6 percent of the locker contents by weight [S2].
- Staff have expanded the program to two more towns [S1].

## Next steps
- Ask the auditor to estimate how much of the locker volume was new recycling rather than diverted depot drop-offs (judgment).

## Sources
- [S1] Harlow County Department of Environmental Services, Battery Locker Pilot Final Report (August 2026)
- [S2] Harlow County Auditor, Review of Battery Locker Pilot (September 2026)
